## Learning goals

- See when MLE fails with small $n$.
- Treat $\theta$ as a random variable with a **prior**, form the **posterior**, take its **mode** (MAP).
- Choose a **conjugate prior**; work the Bernoulli–Beta example.
- Relate MAP $\to$ MLE as $n\to\infty$.

---

## Before this clicks

**MLE** treats $\theta$ as an unknown constant and maximizes $p(x\mid\theta)$. With tiny data, that can be silly: four coin tosses all heads $\Rightarrow\hat\theta_{\mathrm{ML}}=1$ even if you know the coin is not two-headed.

**Prior** $p(\theta)$: belief about $\theta$ **before** seeing data. **Posterior** $p(\theta\mid x)\propto p(x\mid\theta)\,p(\theta)$: updated belief.

---

## Main ideas

### 1. Bayesian parameter estimation (idea)

Assume $\theta\sim p(\theta)$. After data $x$,

$$
p(\theta\mid x) \;\propto\; p(x\mid\theta)\,p(\theta).
$$

You get a **whole distribution** over $\theta$, not a single point. For building one Bayes classifier you often need one number: take the **mode**

$$
\theta_{\mathrm{MAP}} = \arg\max_\theta\, p(\theta\mid x) = \arg\max_\theta\, p(x\mid\theta)\,p(\theta).
$$

(Equivalently maximize $\log p(x\mid\theta)+\log p(\theta)$.)

### 2. Conjugate priors

A prior is **conjugate** for a likelihood if the posterior stays in the **same family** as the prior. Motivation: parameter support/structure should not jump families just because you saw data (Bernoulli parameter stays on $(0,1)$; Beta$\to$Beta).

### 3. Example: Bernoulli with Beta prior

Likelihood (one flip): $p(x\mid\theta)=\theta^x(1-\theta)^{1-x}$.

Beta prior:

$$
p(\theta) \propto \theta^{\alpha-1}(1-\theta)^{\beta-1},\qquad \theta\in(0,1).
$$

Posterior $\propto \theta^{x+\alpha-1}(1-\theta)^{\beta-x}$ — still Beta (conjugate). Mode (for suitable $\alpha,\beta$):

$$
\theta_{\mathrm{MAP}} = \frac{x+\alpha-1}{\alpha+\beta-2}
$$

(for one sample; with $n$ i.i.d. flips, replace $x$ by $\sum_i x_i$ and adjust the denominator with $n$).

Compare to $\theta_{\mathrm{ML}}=\bar x$. Extra $\alpha,\beta$ “pseudo-counts” pull the estimate toward the prior. As $n\to\infty$, MAP $\to$ MLE (data washes out the prior).

Uniform prior (special Beta) recovers MLE.

### 4. Full Bayes vs MAP (preview)

MAP collapses the posterior to one point. **Fully Bayesian** methods keep $p(\theta\mid x)$ and push uncertainty into predictions (e.g. Bayesian neural nets). Later: MAP $\leftrightarrow$ **regularization** in the ERM view.

### 5. Link to nonparametric next

Sometimes you only need $p(x)$ **at a query point**, not a global parametric form — Parzen / nearest-neighbor density estimates.

---

## Worked mini-example

Fair-coin belief: Beta$(\alpha,\beta)$ peaked near $1/2$. Data: three heads, one tail. MLE $=3/4$. MAP pulls toward $1/2$ depending on $\alpha,\beta$. If all four are heads, MLE $=1$ but MAP $<1$ whenever $\beta>1$.

---

## Common confusions

| Confusion | Clarification |
|-----------|---------------|
| Prior comes from the training set | Prior is **pre-data** belief; data enters only through the likelihood. |
| Posterior family can be anything | Prefer conjugates so support/form stay coherent. |
| MAP uses the posterior mean | MAP = **mode**; for asymmetric posteriors mean $\neq$ mode. |
